# Content mechanism

**What is the reel's engine: teaching, testing, ranking, busting, or a series?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C15


## Tutorial / do-this-now
<a id="tutorial"></a>

Teach one thing the viewer can apply at once, ideally while watching.

**Looks like:** A screen recording of the exact steps, with a circular face cam: 'Change one word in the Gmail URL...'. The result appears on screen and the viewer tries it.

**Good at:** saves; shares; universal reach; trust

**Weak at:** lower like rate from non-followers; easy to copy

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, yt-short, carousel · niches tech, gym, all · goals saves, shares, reach · effort medium

**How:** Screen-record on the PC/iPhone. Show each step with a click SFX and a highlight box in CapCut.

**Backed by:** ["Do this now": a tiny effort, instant payoff](../topics/hooks.md#hook-do-this-now), [Shareability: why would they send it?](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-shareability-test), ["Take a picture" save moment](../topics/growth.md#growth-screenshot-save-moment), [Pick one goal: comments, sends or saves](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-conversation-goal), [Context in the first words, three channels](../topics/hooks.md#hook-context-first-words) · sources R1, L07, L04

## Myth-bust / proof reel
<a id="myth-bust"></a>

Quote a myth, then disprove it, ideally with a physical demo.

**Looks like:** Text: 'Pilates won't make you stronger.' A weighted plank is already in motion. 6–18 s, with the text on screen the whole time and a loop-friendly end.

**Good at:** thumb stop; comments; short and loopable

**Weak at:** a debunk with no takeaway underperformed for Rahul; needs real proof

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short · niches gym, tech · goals comments, reach · effort low

**How:** One or two shots on a tripod, bold quote text in Edits, trending audio low under it.

**Backed by:** [Industry trope, then your contrary view](../topics/story.md#story-industry-contrarian), [Universal tricks reach, niche builds engage](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-universal-vs-niche-reach), [Lean: proof, pain/benefit or shock](../topics/hooks.md#hook-lean-three-ways), ["8 Mile": disprove the counter-argument first](../topics/story.md#story-8-mile), [Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline) · sources research, L05, R1

## Challenge / experiment
<a id="challenge-experiment"></a>

A clear premise you test: 'I tried X for 7 days', 'X vs Y', 'I tested the cheapest...'.

**Looks like:** Cold open on the most extreme moment, then 'let's find out'. Stages with a scoreboard or day counter, and a verdict at the end.

**Good at:** retention; follows (people want the result); long form

**Weak at:** takes days to film; the result may be boring

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-long · niches gym, tech, gaming · goals retention, follows · effort high

**How:** Plan the stages and film each with the same angle and light. Add a HyperFrames scoreboard or day counter. Hook template (L11): 'I'm going to [X] for [Y] days straight' (example: study 8 hours, 5 days straight, 4.9M).

**Backed by:** [Series get the best view-to-follower ratio](../topics/growth.md#growth-series-view-to-follower), [Open loops, re-open one at ~15 s](../topics/story.md#story-open-loops), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [70 / 20 / 10 proven, iterate, experiment](../topics/growth.md#growth-70-20-10), [Outlines and mechanisms: blitz, storytime, opinions](../topics/story.md#story-controversial-outline) · sources research, L08, L11

## Rating, tier list or versus
<a id="rating-versus"></a>

Score things, rank them, or put two against each other.

**Looks like:** Product card, price, then the x/10 reveal with a one-word label ('HEATER'). Or '6 ways A beats B', posted with the mirror version 48 h later.

**Good at:** comments (people disagree); saves; clear structure; repeatable format

**Weak at:** needs credible judgement; can feel like a list

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short, carousel · niches tech, gym, gaming · goals comments, saves · effort medium

**How:** Score cards and tier tables in HyperFrames, or CapCut text with a pop SFX per score. Hook template (L11): 'Rating [X] so you don't waste your [Y]' (example: supplements / money, S–F tier board, 4.7M).

**Backed by:** [Verdict first: name, price, score](../topics/hooks.md#hook-verdict-first), [Compare new things to known ones](../topics/text.md#text-compare-to-known), [Live-build parts card with budget bar](../topics/effects.md#fx-live-build-parts-card), [Challenge, ranking and list templates](../topics/hooks.md#l11-classic-hook-templates), [Sponsor as the "pro" answer](../topics/business.md#biz-sponsor-as-smart-option) · sources R1, L07, L09, research, L11

## Series / monthly franchise
<a id="series"></a>

Recurring episodes: 'Day X of...', or a dated franchise like '₹X PC Build – October 2026'.

**Looks like:** Same opener, same angle, same title style every episode, with a day counter or month label. The ending says 'follow along'. Each episode stands alone but rewards followers.

**Good at:** best view-to-follower ratio; follows; easy ideation; refreshable

**Weak at:** needs commitment; fatigue if the format never changes

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals follows, retention · effort medium

**How:** Build a template project in CapCut or a HyperFrames title card with the day or month as a variable.

**Backed by:** [Series get the best view-to-follower ratio](../topics/growth.md#growth-series-view-to-follower), [Monthly franchise and a running storyline](../topics/growth.md#growth-monthly-franchise), [14 topics, then reformat them](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-14-topics-reformatted), [Brand world: characters, sets, plot](../topics/brand.md#brand-world-characters-sets), [Promise hook: daily habit, three payoffs](../topics/hooks.md#l11-promise-hook) · sources L08, L05, R1

## Mixing
A series of tutorials or ratings (Rahul's monthly builds) combines two engines. A myth-bust is often the hook of a tutorial.

## Rule of thumb
Saves and shares: tutorial. Follows: series or experiment. Comments: rating/versus or myth-bust (with a takeaway).
